outline: 68 Projectile Motion and Velocity as a Vector
190 Deriving the Six Equations of Motion

examples.question_text: A ball is projected from level ground at $24\text{ m/s}$ at $30^\circ$ above the horizontal. Take $g=10\text{ m/s}^2$. Find (a) the time to reach its greatest height, (b) its greatest height, (c) the time of flight, (d) the range and (e) its impact speed and direction.

A stone is thrown from a high cliff with initial velocity $12\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j}\text{ m/s}$. It is still in flight after $1$ second. Take $g=10\text{ m/s}^2$. Find its speed and direction at that time, giving the angle to $1$ decimal place.
examples.solution_text:
The initial vertical component is negative because the stone is thrown downwards.
$\begin{align*}\dot{x}&=12\\\dot{y}&=-5-10t\\\dot{y}(1)&=-5-10(1)\\&=-15.\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}\text{Speed}&=\sqrt{12^2+(-15)^2}\\&=3\sqrt{41}\text{ m/s},\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{15}{12}\right)\\&\approx51.3^\circ.\end{align*}$
The stone moves at $3\sqrt{41}\text{ m/s}$ at $51.3^\circ$ below the horizontal.

For horizontal projection, $\dot{y}(0)=0$.
$\begin{align*}\dot{x}&=16,&x&=16t,\\\dot{y}&=-10t,&y&=-5t^2.\end{align*}$
(a) The ground is at $y=-45$.
$\begin{align*}-45&=-5t^2\\t^2&=9\\t&=3\text{ s}.\end{align*}$
The negative root is outside the flight.
(b) The horizontal distance is
$\begin{align*}x(3)&=16(3)\\&=48\text{ m}.\end{align*}$
(c) At impact, $\dot{x}=16$ and $\dot{y}=-30$.
$\begin{align*}\text{Speed}&=\sqrt{16^2+(-30)^2}\\&=34\text{ m/s},\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{30}{16}\right)\\&\approx61.9^\circ.\end{align*}$
The ball strikes the ground at $34\text{ m/s}$ at $61.9^\circ$ below the horizontal.

examples.question_text: A ball is thrown from a $60\text{ m}$ platform at $30\text{ m/s}$ at an angle $\theta$ above the horizontal, where $\tan\theta=\frac{3}{4}$. Take the launch point as the origin and $g=10\text{ m/s}^2$. Find (a) the time of flight, (b) the horizontal distance from the base to its landing point, (c) its greatest height above the ground and (d) its impact speed. Give non-exact results to $2$ decimal places.
examples.solution_text:
Since $\cos\theta=\frac45$ and $\sin\theta=\frac35$,
$\begin{align*}\dot{x}&=24,&x&=24t,\\\dot{y}&=18-10t,&y&=18t-5t^2.\end{align*}$
(a) The ground is at $y=-60$.
$\begin{align*}-60&=18t-5t^2\\5t^2-18t-60&=0\\t&=\frac{18\pm\sqrt{1524}}{10}\\t&=\frac{9+\sqrt{381}}5\approx5.70\text{ s}.\end{align*}$
Only the positive root is during the flight.
(b) Use the exact landing time $T=\frac{9+\sqrt{381}}5$.
$\begin{align*}x(T)&=\frac{24(9+\sqrt{381})}{5}\\&\approx136.89\text{ m}.\end{align*}$
(c) At greatest height, $\dot{y}=0$.
$\begin{align*}0&=18-10t\\t&=1.8\text{ s},\\y(1.8)&=18(1.8)-5(1.8)^2\\&=16.2\text{ m}.\end{align*}$
The greatest height above the ground is $60+16.2=76.2\text{ m}$.
(d) Substitute the exact landing time into the vertical velocity.
$\begin{align*}\dot{y}(T)&=18-10\left(\frac{9+\sqrt{381}}5\right)\\&=-2\sqrt{381},\\\text{Impact speed}&=\sqrt{24^2+(-2\sqrt{381})^2}\\&=10\sqrt{21}\text{ m/s}\\&\approx45.83\text{ m/s}.\end{align*}$

The downward initial vertical component is $-20\sin30^\circ=-10\text{ m/s}$.
$\begin{align*}\dot{y}&=-10-10t\\y&=-10t-5t^2.\end{align*}$
At the ground, $y=-30$.
$\begin{align*}-30&=-10t-5t^2\\t^2+2t-6&=0\\t&=-1\pm\sqrt7.\end{align*}$
Reject the negative root. The stone reaches the ground after $(\sqrt7-1)\text{ s}$.

examples.question_text: A ball is projected from level ground at $30\sqrt2\text{ m/s}$ at $45^\circ$ above the horizontal. Take $g=10\text{ m/s}^2$. Find its speed and direction when it is $40\text{ m}$ above the ground, giving the angle to $2$ decimal places.
examples.solution_text:
The equations needed are
$\begin{align*}\dot{x}&=30\\\dot{y}&=30-10t\\y&=30t-5t^2.\end{align*}$
First find both times at height $40\text{ m}$.
$\begin{align*}40&=30t-5t^2\\t^2-6t+8&=0\\(t-2)(t-4)&=0\\t&=2\text{ or }4\text{ s}.\end{align*}$
Substitute each time into the vertical velocity.
$\begin{align*}\dot{y}(2)&=30-10(2)=10\\\dot{y}(4)&=30-10(4)=-10.\end{align*}$
At either time,
$\begin{align*}\text{Speed}&=\sqrt{30^2+10^2}\\&=10\sqrt{10}\text{ m/s},\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{10}{30}\right)\\&\approx18.43^\circ.\end{align*}$
The ball moves at $10\sqrt{10}\text{ m/s}$ at $18.43^\circ$ above the horizontal while rising, or $18.43^\circ$ below it while falling.

examples.question_text: Two stones are thrown simultaneously from the same point on level ground at $28\text{ m/s}$. One is projected at $30^\circ$ and the other at $60^\circ$ above the horizontal. Take $g=10\text{ m/s}^2$. Which stone lands first, and by how long? Give the time difference to $1$ decimal place.
examples.solution_text:
For the $30^\circ$ stone,
$\begin{align*}y_{30}&=28\sin30^\circ\,t-5t^2\\&=14t-5t^2.\end{align*}$
At landing,
$\begin{align*}0&=t(14-5t)\\T_{30}&=\frac{14}{5}\text{ s}.\end{align*}$
For the $60^\circ$ stone,
$\begin{align*}y_{60}&=28\sin60^\circ\,t-5t^2\\&=14\sqrt3\,t-5t^2.\end{align*}$
At landing,
$\begin{align*}0&=t(14\sqrt3-5t)\\T_{60}&=\frac{14\sqrt3}{5}\text{ s}.\end{align*}$
In each case, $t=0$ is the launch.
$\begin{align*}T_{60}-T_{30}&=\frac{14(\sqrt3-1)}5\\&\approx2.0\text{ s}.\end{align*}$
The $30^\circ$ stone lands first, by $2.0\text{ s}$.

coverage.summary: Authored seven worked examples covering all distinct retained assessment methods, including horizontal, upward and downward platform launches. Adapted supplied booklet tasks with different values and checked the new working against its taught methods. Questions and solutions are separate editable fields; prose inherits blue solution styling, mathematics uses single-dollar aligned spans, and diagrams contain explicit 10 pt labels. No existing examples were supplied. Assessments were classified only, without alteration or repeated mathematical audit. Independent review and actual rendered visual verification remain pending.

examples.derivation: Initial components are (12√3,12). Vertical velocity vanishes at t=1.2 s, giving H=7.2 m. The positive root of 12t−5t²=0 is T=2.4 s, giving R=28.8√3 m. Impact components are (12√3,−12), giving speed 24 m/s and direction 30° below horizontal. The plotted path has its vertex at (14.4√3,7.2) and lands at x=28.8√3, consistent with its annotations. Adaptation matches source lines 676–721.

At t=1 s, velocity components are (12,−15). Speed is √369=3√41 m/s; the angle below horizontal is arctan(15/12)=51.340…°, rounding to 51.3°. The stated in-flight condition makes evaluation valid. Component substitution and downward signs match source lines 913–939 and 1406–1422. No diagram is necessary.

Horizontal projection gives y=−5t². Setting y=−45 gives T=3 s, rejecting −3 s. Horizontal distance is 16×3=48 m. Impact components (16,−30) give speed √1156=34 m/s and angle arctan(30/16)=61.927…°, rounding to 61.9° below horizontal. The question diagram shows only the supplied height, horizontal launch velocity and launch origin. Adaptation matches source lines 1334–1344.

Resolving gives initial components (24,18). Landing satisfies 5t²−18t−60=0, whose positive root is T=(9+√381)/5=5.703844… s. Range is 24T=136.892258… m. The highest point occurs at t=1.8 s, with rise 16.2 m and height above ground 76.2 m. Impact vertical velocity is −2√381; speed is √(576+1524)=10√21=45.825756… m/s. All rounding is correct. Methods match source lines 1181–1234 and 1463–1493. A diagram is not required to resolve the explicitly stated origin and ground level.

Initial vertical velocity is −20sin30°=−10 m/s, giving y=−10t−5t². Landing at y=−30 gives t²+2t−6=0 and roots −1±√7. The positive flight time is √7−1 s. The diagram's launch vector points 30° below horizontal and shows the supplied tower height without answer annotations. Adaptation matches source lines 1406–1432.

Initial components are (30,30). Height 40 m gives t²−6t+8=0, so t=2 or 4 s; both occur before landing at 6 s. Vertical velocities are +10 and −10 m/s respectively. Speed at either time is √1000=10√10 m/s. Direction magnitude is arctan(1/3)=18.434948…°, giving 18.43° above horizontal while rising and below horizontal while falling. This follows the supplied velocity-at-height task at lines 778–783. No diagram is necessary.

Positive landing times are T30=14/5=2.8 s and T60=14√3/5=4.849742… s. Their difference is 14(√3−1)/5=2.049742… s, rounding to 2.0 s. The 30° stone lands first. Separate landing equations and subtraction match source lines 1079–1103. No diagram is necessary.
